transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Well, I'm here because the medical clinic for this new logistics job I'm trying to get said my weight was too low to clear me for work. Which is just... I don't know, it's ridiculous. To me, I just look lean, you know? Like someone who's ready to work, stay quick on his feet. You gotta be quick on your feet in freight. I remember back in '98, I was working this dock job in Seattle, and man, the guys who were heavy, they just couldn't keep up. We had this one guy, big guy, always sweating through his shirt by 9 AM. He ended up dropping a whole pallet of electronics because he couldn't move out of the way fast enough when the forklift backed up. Cost the company thousands. Anyway, yeah, they sent me here because of the weight thing, but I think they just don't understand what it takes to actually do the job right.
Have you lost any weight recently without trying to, or have you noticed that you're eating less than usual?

I mean, trying to lose it? No, not really. But eating less... I guess so. Most days I just keep it to black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna. And if I’m not actually moving freight on a shift, I tell myself I don’t need a real meal anyway, you know? You don't put gas in a truck that's just sitting in the lot. 

Speaking of trucks, my buddy Carl down at the yard—he's this diesel mechanic, knows everything about engines—he was trying to tell me I need to start running premium in my '04 Tacoma. I told him, Carl, it's a Tacoma. It'll run on spit and dirt. But he’s always trying to get me to spend money on things I don't need. Same guy who bought a twenty-foot pontoon boat right before the 2008 crash. Man, you should have seen his face when the repo guys showed up. We were actually having a couple beers on his lawn when they backed the hitch right up to his driveway. It was wild. He tried to argue with them, but they had the paperwork and everything. 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, eating. Yeah, I just don't see the point in eating a real meal if I'm not out there burning it off on the dock. Just makes sense to keep it light.
Have you noticed yourself losing weight without trying, or has this been more about your choice to eat less?

Well, like I said, I'm not really trying to lose it. It just happens when you're eating light. And I choose to eat light because, you know, I'm not working right now. It's just common sense. 

Actually, speaking of common sense, you wouldn't believe the guys they have running the safety orientations these days. I had to sit through this three-hour video last week for a different warehouse job, and the guy in the video—I swear he looked like he'd never lifted a box in his life. He was wearing these pristine, brand-new steel-toe boots. Not a scuff on them! You can always tell a guy who doesn't actually work the floor by his boots. My boots, I've had them since... man, maybe 2015? Red Wings. Best boots you can buy. I had to get them resoled twice, but they mold right to your feet. There was this guy I worked with in Portland, Jimmy, he bought cheap boots off the internet and ended up dropping a crate of auto parts right on his foot. Broke three toes. He was out for six weeks, and when he came back, they put him on inventory duty with a clipboard. He hated it. 

But yeah, I don't know if I'm losing weight without trying or what. I just eat what I think I need for the day, which isn't much if I'm just sitting around waiting for this medical clearance to go through.
Have you noticed your weight going down even when you’ve been eating the same amount or when you haven’t been actively trying to lose weight?

Well, I don't really pay that much attention to the scale, honestly. Like I said, I'm just eating what makes sense for not working. I don't know if it's going down on its own or what. 

You know, the scale at that clinic was one of those old-school balance beam ones with the sliding weights. Reminded me of my high school wrestling days back in Spokane. Coach Miller used to make us weigh in before every practice. He was a hardass, but a good guy. He actually ended up opening a sporting goods store downtown after he retired from teaching. I went in there a few years ago to buy some fishing gear—I like to go out to the lakes when I have time, mostly for trout. Caught a real nice rainbow trout up near Mount Baker once, must have been about four pounds. Fought like crazy. I was using this old spinning reel my dad gave me, the drag was all messed up, so I had to pull it in almost entirely by hand. Took me twenty minutes. By the time I got it in the net, my arms were burning. 

But yeah, I haven't really noticed my weight doing anything weird. Just seems normal for what I'm eating.
Have you noticed your weight going down even when you haven't been eating less or trying to lose weight?

Doc, I feel like you keep asking me the exact same thing. Like I've been saying, if my weight is going down, it's because I'm eating less since I'm off the floor. It's not just dropping off me by magic while I'm eating big meals, you know? I haven't noticed anything like that. 

Speaking of weight, though, you should see the tricks some of these owner-operator truckers pull to get under the limit at the DOT weigh stations out on I-90. I used to ride along with my uncle when I was in my twenties, and those DOT guys do not mess around. My uncle got hit with a huge fine once because his rear axle was over the limit. Turns out the loaders at the yard didn't distribute the pallets right. You gotta put the heavier freight forward, but these kids they hire just shove it in wherever it fits so they can go on break. My uncle was so mad, he actually made the dispatcher drive all the way out to the weigh station to look at it himself. The dispatcher drove this beat-up old Ford Taurus, missing a hubcap on the front left side, and the transmission slipped every time he hit forty. He had to take the back roads the whole way there. 

But yeah, to answer your question again, no. My weight isn't just dropping on its own. It's just tied to what I put in the tank.
Have you found yourself not wanting to eat even when you're not consciously trying to eat less or not feeling hungry at all?

Well, no, not really. I mean, if I'm not eating, it's just because I know I don't need it right now. I don't really get that feeling where I just don't want to eat for no reason. 

You know, talking about not wanting to eat, it reminds me of this diner we used to hit up outside of Missoula. The Silver Skillet, I think it was called. They had this meatloaf special on Thursdays that was just... man, it was legendary. But then they changed management back in, I wanna say, 2018? The new guy decided to cut costs and started using this cheap filler in the meatloaf. You could taste it right away. It had this weird, almost spongy texture. I took one bite and pushed the plate away. The waitress—Brenda, she'd been there for like twenty years, always had her hair up in this big beehive thing—she knew immediately. She didn't even charge me for it. She just sighed and said, "I know, honey, it's not the same." She actually ended up quitting a few months later and went to work at a bakery down the street. I went in there once to get a coffee and she gave me a free bear claw. Best pastry I ever had. 

But no, I don't just lose my appetite for no reason. It's all just about matching what I eat to what I'm doing.
Have you ever found yourself not feeling hungry for several days in a row, even when you haven’t been trying to eat less or cut back on food?

No, I can't say I've ever just gone days and days without feeling hungry for no reason. 

Speaking of days in a row, though... man, back in ninety-eight, we had this massive backlog at the freight yard in Tacoma. A bunch of guys called out sick with some flu bug, so they had the rest of us pulling double shifts, three days straight. It was brutal. My foreman, this guy named Gary, he was practically living in his little glass office on the floor. He brought in this giant percolator, must have held fifty cups of coffee, just to keep us all moving. And he ordered these huge party subs from a deli down the street so we would not have to leave the yard. Problem was, by the second day, the lettuce would get all slimy and the bread was just soaking wet with oil and vinegar. You'd pick a piece up and it would just fall apart in your hands. We had this one forklift driver, a kid named Toby, who tried to eat it anyway and ended up throwing up behind a stack of dog food pallets. Gary didn't even send him home, he just pointed at the janitor closet and told him to grab a mop. 

But uh... yeah, hunger. No, I definitely feel it if I go too long. I just don't let it dictate things, you know? I just eat what I need for the work I'm doing.
Have you ever found yourself not being interested in food or not wanting to eat, even when you weren’t making a conscious choice to eat less or weren’t trying to stay lean?

No, not really. I mean, I'm just not interested in eating if I'm not doing anything that requires the energy. It's not like I just lose interest in food out of nowhere. 

You know, talking about not being interested in food... my ex-wife, Sarah, she went through this phase where she got super into these weird diets. Like, one month it was only things you could blend, and the next month it was just cabbage soup. She bought this industrial-strength blender, sounded like a jet engine taking off in the kitchen every morning at six a.m. The dog used to hide under the couch. Anyway, she made me try this kale and beet smoothie once. I took one sip and I swear it tasted like dirt and pennies. I told her I wasn't interested, and she got so mad she didn't talk to me for two days. She ended up throwing the whole pitcher in the sink and it stained the porcelain this weird pink color. We had to use bleach on it for weeks. She actually tried to paint over it once with this appliance touch-up paint, but it didn't match the rest of the sink at all. Looked like a big white bandage right next to the drain. 

But yeah, to get back to what you were asking... no, I don't just lose interest in food. It's just a practical thing for me.
Have you ever found yourself not wanting to eat or having no interest in food, even when you weren't trying to control your weight or adjust your eating based on how much you were working?

Well, no, I don't think so. Like I said, I don't just lose my appetite out of nowhere. If I'm not eating, it's just 'cause my body doesn't need the fuel for the work I'm doing. It's not a lack of interest, it's just... math, I guess. 

You know, talking about adjusting fuel for the work, it actually reminds me of this old Hyster forklift we used to run at the warehouse down in Kent. This thing was an absolute dinosaur. It ran on propane, but the fuel gauge on the dash was completely busted. You never actually knew how much was in the tank, so you just had to guess based on how heavy your loads were that shift. Well, we hired this new kid, maybe nineteen, and he didn't swap the tank before starting a big unloading job. He was right in the middle of lifting a double-stacked pallet of ceramic bathroom tiles—really heavy stuff, you know?—and the engine just sputters and dies. The hydraulics locked up, the forks tilted, and smash. Thousands of dollars of tile just shattered all over the concrete dock. 

My supervisor, Rick, he came running out of the office, took one look at the mess, and kicked the forklift tire so hard he broke his big toe. He had to wear this giant black medical boot for like two months. Just clomping around the warehouse all day, complaining to anyone who would listen about how his wife was making him sleep on the couch because he wouldn't take the boot off in bed. 

But uh, what were we saying? Yeah, food. No, I don't just lose interest in it for no reason. If I need the energy, I eat. If I don't, I don't. Simple as that.
Have you ever found yourself not wanting to eat or having no interest in food even when you weren’t adjusting your eating based on work or trying to stay lean?

I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again, doc. Like I've been saying, no, I don't just lose my appetite for the heck of it. It's not like that. It's just fuel. 

Speaking of losing things, though... man, you want to talk about losing something. My buddy Dave, we were working the graveyard shift down at the railyard back in '04. He had this bad habit of taking his wedding ring off when he was operating the winch, said the metal pinched his finger against the lever. Anyway, one night he sets it on the bumper of this flatbed we were loading, completely forgets about it, and the truck pulls out heading for Spokane. Dave realizes about twenty minutes later and just completely loses his mind. He actually clocked out, got in his own car, and tried to chase the rig down I-90. Got pulled over by a state trooper doing ninety-five in a sixty zone. The cop didn't care about the ring, just wrote him a massive ticket. And the worst part? His wife found out about the ticket before he even told her about the ring because the court notice came in the mail. Man, she locked him out of the house for a week. He was sleeping in his Honda Civic in the employee lot, using his heavy winter coat as a blanket. 

But anyway... no. I don't lose interest in food. I just eat what I need to get the job done, that's all.
Have you ever found yourself not wanting to eat or having no interest in food, even when you weren’t thinking about work or trying to manage your weight?

Doc, are you pulling my leg? Because I swear you've asked me this exact same question like four times now. I really don't know how else to explain it to you—no. I don't just lose interest in food. It doesn't happen like that for me. 

You know, all this repeating yourself... it actually reminds me of this old '89 Chevy Cheyenne I used to drive for a landscaping outfit back in the nineties. The cassette deck in that truck was completely jammed. It had a Bob Seger tape stuck in it, and the auto-reverse was busted, so it just played the same three songs on a loop, all day, every day. Drove my buddy Mike absolutely up the wall. We were hauling a load of mulch out to Bellevue one afternoon, and Mike just snaps. He grabs a flathead screwdriver out of the glovebox and starts prying at the radio panel while I'm doing sixty-five down the highway. He jams it in there, sparks literally fly out of the dash, and he shorts out the whole electrical system. Blew the fuse for the windshield wipers right as this massive rainstorm hits. We had to pull over under an overpass and sit there for three hours waiting for the rain to stop. Mike ended up falling asleep against the window, and he snores like a chainsaw, so I had to sit there listening to that instead of Bob Seger. Honestly, I think I preferred the tape. 

But seriously, doc, I don't know what you're fishing for here. I don't just forget to want food or lose interest in it. If I'm not eating, it's just 'cause I'm not burning it off. That's really all there is to it.
Have you ever found yourself not wanting to eat or having no interest in food, even when you weren’t thinking about work or trying to manage your weight?

Look, doc, I gotta ask... is there an echo in here? I feel like we're just spinning our tires in the mud now. I don't know how many different ways I can say it. No. I don't just lose my appetite or stop caring about food. It just doesn't happen. 

Honestly, this whole back-and-forth is starting to remind me of old man Higgins. He was the nighttime dispatcher when I drove for Puget Sound Freight back in the day. Guy was pushing seventy, stubborn as a mule, and completely deaf in his left ear, but he flat-out refused to get a hearing aid. Said they were a scam by the government to track your thoughts, or some nonsense like that. Anyway, you'd be out on a run, and he'd radio you the same pickup order three, four times. One night, he sent me and two other drivers to pick up the exact same load of scrap steel from a yard down in Tacoma. We all show up within twenty minutes of each other, blocking the whole street with these massive flatbeds. The yard manager comes out screaming his head off, threatening to call the cops because we're blocking his gates. Higgins wouldn't even admit he messed up! He blamed it on the radio static. After that, we had to start calling his cell phone from a payphone just to make sure he actually heard us. 

But look, to answer your question again... no. I don't have that issue. I don't just forget to eat or lose interest. If I'm not hauling, I don't need the calories. Simple.
Have you ever lost weight even when you were eating enough or when you weren’t trying to eat less?

No, I can't say I have. If I'm eating, I'm maintaining. If I'm losing weight, it's because I'm not putting the fuel in. It's basic math, really. 

Speaking of math, though... you know, it's funny how people just can't do it anymore. My nephew, Tommy, he just got a job working the register at this hardware store out in Renton. Good kid, but man, if the computer goes down, he's completely helpless. I was in there a couple weeks ago buying some lag bolts and a new framing hammer. Total comes to, I don't know, twenty-eight bucks and some change. I hand him two twenties and a handful of nickels and dimes so I can just get a ten back, right? You should have seen the look of absolute panic on his face. He just stared at the coins in my hand like I handed him a live grenade. He actually had to pull out his phone and use the calculator app to figure out the change. I told his dad, my brother, I said, "You gotta teach this kid how to count back change, it's embarrassing." But my brother just laughed it off, said everything's on cards or phones now anyway. Which, I guess he's right, but what happens when the power goes out? You're just gonna stand there staring at each other? It's crazy. 

But yeah, no. To answer your question, no. I've never just lost weight for no reason while eating plenty. It doesn't work like that for me.
Have you ever lost weight even when you were eating normally or when you weren’t cutting back on food at all?

Doc, come on now. Didn't we just cover this? Are you testing me or something? No. I haven't lost weight while eating normally. Like I just said, if I eat, I stay the same. If I don't, I lose. 

Honestly, all this repeating the same thing over and over... it's like dealing with the DMV. You ever try to renew a commercial license down at the branch in Kent? Absolute nightmare. I went down there last month because my medical card was expiring. I get in line, wait forty-five minutes just to talk to the person at the front desk, and she tells me I need form DL-something-or-other. I fill it out, get back in line, wait another hour. Finally get to the window, and the guy looks at it and says, "Oh, you filled out the blue form. You need the green form for a Class A." I swear, my blood pressure spiked so hard I thought I was gonna stroke out right there. I asked him why the lady at the front gave me the blue one, and he just shrugs and says, "She's new." So I had to start the whole process over. Took me four and a half hours just to hand them a piece of paper my doctor already signed. It's like they design the system specifically to drive you crazy. 

But look, I'm telling you straight—no. I don't just magically drop pounds when I'm eating regular meals. It doesn't happen.
Have you ever noticed that you're losing weight even when you're eating regularly and not cutting back on food at all?

Doc, are you pulling my leg here? I mean, seriously. We literally just went over this. No. I don't lose weight if I'm eating normally. It's the same answer I gave you two minutes ago. 

You know, this is exactly what happened when I tried to get my roof patched last fall. I called this guy, Dave... or maybe it was Dan? Anyway, he comes out, looks at the roof, and I tell him, "Look, the leak is right above the master bathroom. Just fix that spot." He nods, writes it down, says he's got it. Two days later, his crew shows up, and they start tearing shingles off over the garage. I run out there, waving my arms, like, "What are you doing? The leak is on the other side of the house!" And the foreman looks at his clipboard and says, "Work order says garage." I had to call Dave—or Dan, whatever his name was—and explain it to him all over again. And you know what he said? "Oh, I must have written it down wrong." Cost me an extra two hundred bucks just for them to put the shingles back on the garage before they even started on the bathroom. It's like nobody actually listens to the words coming out of your mouth anymore. They just hear what they want to hear or follow some script in their head. 

But yeah. No. I don't lose weight when I'm eating regular meals. I really don't know how else to say it.
Have you ever lost weight even when you were eating enough food or when you weren’t intentionally eating less?

Doc, I... I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here. Are you reading off a card or something? Because I swear, if you ask me this one more time, I'm gonna think I'm on a hidden camera show. No. The answer is still no. I don't lose weight if I'm eating enough. 

It's like... it's like talking to my ex-wife, honestly. I'd tell her, "Barb, don't put the cast iron skillet in the dishwasher, it ruins the seasoning." And she'd look right at me, nod, and say, "Okay, got it." Two days later? I open the dishwasher, and there's my grandmother's Griswold skillet, rusted to hell and back. I'd ask her why she did it, and she'd just say, "Oh, I forgot," or "I didn't think it mattered this time." It's like the words just went in one ear, took a little vacation in her brain, and flew right out the other side. Drove me up a wall. I spent three days scrubbing that pan with coarse salt and oil, trying to get it back to normal. You can't just treat cast iron like regular pots and pans, you know? It takes years to build up that non-stick surface, and one cycle in a Maytag just strips it right down to the bare metal. 

Anyway. No. I don't lose weight unless I'm actively not eating. Same as the last three times you asked.
